pharm: Synthetic analogue of arginine vasopressin with potent antidiuretic activity and minimal pressor effect; also raises factor VIII and von Willebrand factor.
quick: Central DI: 0.05 mg PO BID, titrate (usual 0.1-0.8 mg/day divided)
May take with or without food; observe fluid restriction
Generally considered usable when indicated; clinician judgment
Considered compatible; minimal transfer to milk
Serum sodium, fluid balance, urine volume/osmolality
summary: Desmopressin is a synthetic vasopressin analogue used for central diabetes insipidus, temporary polyuria/polydipsia after pituitary surgery or head trauma, and primary nocturnal enuresis. Its main hazard is water intoxication with hyponatremia, which can be fatal; fluid intake must be restricted and serum sodium monitored, especially in children and the elderly. It is ineffective in nephrogenic diabetes insipidus and is contraindicated in moderate-to-severe renal impairment, hyponatremia, or a history of hyponatremia.
indications: Antidiuretic replacement in central (cranial) diabetes insipidus
Temporary polyuria and polydipsia after head trauma or pituitary-region surgery
(Also used clinically for bleeding in mild hemophilia A and type 1 von Willebrand disease - parenteral/intranasal forms)

dosage.n: Usual range 0.1-0.8 mg/day in divided doses; individualize

dosage.d: Begin tablets 12 hours after last intranasal dose
0.2 mg at bedtime, titrate up to 0.6 mg
dosage.n: Limit fluids from 1 h before to 8 h after dose
Do not use in moderate-to-severe renal impairment

admin: Strict fluid restriction during therapy to prevent water intoxication/hyponatremia
For enuresis, limit fluid intake from 1 hour before until 8 hours after the dose
Titrate dose to achieve adequate but not excessive water turnover and adequate sleep duration
When switching from intranasal to oral, start the tablet 12 hours after the last spray
Observe closely during initial titration with safety labs
moa: Acts on renal V2 receptors to increase water reabsorption in the collecting ducts, concentrating urine and reducing urine volume; structural modification of vasopressin enhances antidiuretic potency and duration while minimizing pressor (V1) activity. Also increases plasma factor VIII and von Willebrand factor by endothelial release.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to desmopressin or excipients
Moderate to severe renal impairment (CrCl <50 mL/min)
Hyponatremia or a history of hyponatremia
relative: Conditions with fluid/electrolyte imbalance (cystic fibrosis, heart failure)

preg: Generally considered acceptable when indicated; extensive use in pregnant women with diabetes insipidus has not shown clear fetal harm. Use under clinician supervision.
lact: Minimal amounts in breast milk and poorly absorbed orally by the infant; considered compatible with breastfeeding.
renal: Contraindicated in moderate to severe renal impairment (CrCl below 50 mL/min); renal function affects water handling and hyponatremia risk.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment for hepatic impairment.

major: Drugs increasing water-intoxication/hyponatremia risk - tricyclic antidepressants, SSRIs, chlorpromazine, opioid analgesics, NSAIDs, lamotrigine, carbamazepine (use with caution)
moderate: Other pressor agents - use large doses of desmopressin with careful monitoring
Loperamide and other drugs slowing GI transit - may increase oral desmopressin absorption
minor: Demeclocycline, lithium, norepinephrine, heparin, alcohol - may reduce antidiuretic effect
interactions.food: Food may reduce the extent and rate of oral absorption; take consistently and observe fluid limits
interactions.alcohol: Excess fluid/alcohol intake increases risk of water intoxication; avoid
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor serum sodium and urine osmolality/volume to guide therapy.

serious: Hyponatremia and water intoxication (can cause seizures, coma, death)
Symptomatic hyponatremia (headache, nausea/vomiting, weight gain, restlessness, confusion)
emergency: Severe hyponatremia with seizures or coma

monitoring: Serum sodium (baseline and during therapy, especially after dose changes and in elderly/children)
Fluid intake and output; body weight
Urine volume and osmolality for therapeutic response in diabetes insipidus
Signs/symptoms of hyponatremia and water intoxication
Blood pressure with high or parenteral doses
counsel: Limit how much you drink as instructed - too much fluid can be dangerous
For bedwetting, avoid drinking from 1 hour before until 8 hours after the dose
Report headache, nausea, vomiting, weight gain, restlessness, or confusion right away
Skip the dose and call your clinician if you have a stomach bug with vomiting or diarrhea
Do not change the dose on your own
pk: Tablets at room temperature; injection refrigerated per label
pearls: Water intoxication/hyponatremia is the key danger - fluid restriction and sodium monitoring are essential, especially in children and the elderly
Contraindicated in renal impairment (CrCl <50) and in hyponatremia or its history
Also raises factor VIII and vWF - used for mild hemophilia A and type 1 von Willebrand disease
Hold the dose during intercurrent illness with vomiting/diarrhea or excessive fluid intake
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered, unless near the next dose - then skip it. Do not double the dose, and continue to observe fluid limits.
overdose: Overdose causes fluid retention with hyponatremia: confusion, drowsiness, persistent headache, difficulty urinating, and rapid weight gain. There is no specific antidote. Reduce or withhold the dose, restrict fluids, and treat hyponatremia per severity (fluid restriction, and hypertonic saline only with caution for severe symptomatic cases).
